concepts.name: Exchange of virtual particles
concepts.statement: A force is carried by the exchange of virtual particles, created for a short time in temporary violation of the conservation of mass-energy, as the uncertainty principle allows. Such a particle cannot be observed directly, because observing it would take more time than it exists.

concepts.name: Range and carrier mass
concepts.statement: A carrier particle can travel only as far as light goes in the time it may exist, $d \approx c\,\Delta t$, and that time is shorter the greater its mass. The heavier the carrier, the shorter the range of the force it carries.

concepts.name: Estimating a carrier mass
concepts.statement: The mass of a carrier particle is estimated from the range of its force in three steps: the range gives the time the particle may exist, the uncertainty principle turns that time into an energy, and $\Delta E = mc^{2}$ turns the energy into a mass. The same chain runs backward from a mass to a range.

concepts.name: Pions and muons
concepts.statement: The pions, discovered with about the mass Yukawa predicted, carry the strong force between nucleons; the muon, of nearly the same mass, does not feel the strong force at all.

concepts.name: Virtual particle
concepts.statement: A virtual particle is a particle created for a short time in temporary violation of the conservation of mass-energy, as the uncertainty principle allows, and which cannot be observed directly.

concepts.name: Pion
concepts.statement: A pion is the particle exchanged between nucleons that carries the strong nuclear force; it is a meson with a mass about 270 times the electron's.

concepts.name: Meson
concepts.statement: A meson is a particle whose mass is intermediate between the electron and nucleon masses, as the masses of the pions are; the name now covers an entire class of particles.

concepts.name: Properties of the four forces
concepts.statement: The four basic forces differ greatly in strength and range: gravity and the electromagnetic force have infinite range, the weak and strong nuclear forces are short ranged, and each is carried by its own particle, the graviton, the photon, the $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$, and the gluons.

concepts.name: Feynman diagram
concepts.statement: A Feynman diagram is a graph of time against position that shows particles approaching, exchanging virtual particles and leaving.

concepts.name: Quantum electrodynamics
concepts.statement: Quantum electrodynamics is the quantum theory of the electromagnetic force, which it treats as carried by virtual photons and calculates from Feynman diagrams. Every later theory of a force is modeled on it.

concepts.name: Carrier mass and force range
concepts.statement: The four ranges in Table 33.1 follow from one rule: the photon and graviton are massless, so their forces reach any distance, while the $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$, about 1000 times the pion's mass, give the weak force about 1/1000 of the strong force's range.

concepts.name: Gluon
concepts.statement: A gluon is one of eight massless particles that carry the strong force between quarks.

concepts.name: Creation of matter in accelerators
concepts.statement: A collision can create new particles from its energy, $m = \Delta E/c^{2}$, so the more energy an accelerator gives its particles, the heavier the particles it can create, within the conservation laws.

concepts.name: Early accelerators
concepts.statement: The first accelerators were the electrostatic Van de Graaff, which gives particles the energy of a single large voltage, and the cyclotron, which accelerates them across a gap with an alternating voltage of fixed frequency while a magnetic field bends them round again in ever larger circles.

concepts.name: Synchrotron
concepts.statement: A synchrotron is a circular accelerator in which the frequency of the accelerating voltage and the strength of the magnetic field rise as the particles gain energy, so that they keep to an orbit of fixed radius.

concepts.name: Synchrotron radiation
concepts.statement: Synchrotron radiation is the electromagnetic radiation given off by charged particles as a magnetic field bends their path. It costs light particles such as electrons the most energy.

concepts.name: Colliding beams
concepts.statement: A beam striking a fixed target must leave its products recoiling, wasting energy; two beams meeting head-on have zero total momentum, so particles of twice the beam energy can be made.

concepts.name: Finding energy gained across accelerating gaps
concepts.statement: The energy a particle gains across an accelerating gap is $\text{PE}_{\text{elec}} = qV$, so a proton gains 1 eV for each volt it crosses and the energy from a linear accelerator is the sum of its gap voltages.

concepts.name: Van de Graaff accelerator
concepts.statement: A Van de Graaff is an electrostatic accelerator that gives charged particles the energy of the single large voltage it builds up on a charged dome.

concepts.name: Cyclotron
concepts.statement: A cyclotron is an accelerator in which a magnetic field bends charged particles in a spiral while an alternating voltage of fixed frequency accelerates them each time they cross the gap between two hollow D-shaped electrodes.

concepts.name: Linear accelerator
concepts.statement: A linear accelerator accelerates charged particles in a straight line through a series of tubes, giving them energy across the gap between each tube and the next.

concepts.name: Antiparticles and annihilation
concepts.statement: Every particle has an antiparticle with the same mass and the opposite charge, and a particle and its antiparticle can annihilate, turning their whole mass into photons that move apart to keep the total momentum zero.

concepts.name: Hadrons and leptons
concepts.statement: Particles are classified first by the forces they feel: hadrons feel the strong nuclear force and leptons do not. Only six leptons exist and they seem fundamental, while the hadrons are many.

concepts.name: Bosons and fermions
concepts.statement: Particles are divided by spin into bosons, with integral spin, and fermions, with half-integral spin, which obey the exclusion principle. All carrier particles are bosons, while quarks and leptons are fermions.

concepts.name: Conservation of lepton family numbers
concepts.statement: The six leptons fall into three families, the electron, muon and tau families, and in every reaction the total electron family number $L_{e}$, muon family number $L_{\mu}$ and tau family number $L_{\tau}$ are each conserved.

concepts.name: Mesons and baryons
concepts.statement: The hadrons are of two kinds, told apart not by mass but by decay: a meson can decay to leptons and leave no hadron, while a baryon always decays to another baryon.

concepts.name: Conservation of baryon number
concepts.statement: In every reaction the total baryon number is conserved. This is why the proton, the lightest baryon, does not decay, and why the number of nucleons in a nuclear reaction stays the same.

concepts.name: Particle lifetime and force
concepts.statement: The stronger the force that causes a decay, the faster the decay, so a particle's lifetime shows which force is at work: about $10^{-23}$ s for the strong force and $10^{-10}$ s or longer for the weak force. Leptons among the products also point to the weak force.

concepts.name: Strangeness
concepts.statement: Strangeness $S$ is a quantum number given to particles to account for decays that every other conservation law allows but that never happen; it is 0 for the ordinary hadrons and nonzero for the strange particles.

concepts.name: Checking conservation in a decay
concepts.statement: A decay is checked by adding up the charge, baryon number, lepton family numbers and strangeness before and after: a decay that conserves all of them can happen, and one that changes strangeness can happen only through the weak force.

concepts.name: Boson
concepts.statement: A boson is a particle with integral spin, 0, 1, 2 and so on; bosons do not obey the Pauli exclusion principle.

concepts.name: Fermion
concepts.statement: A fermion is a particle with half-integral spin, 1/2, 3/2 and so on; fermions obey the Pauli exclusion principle.

concepts.name: Hadron
concepts.statement: A hadron is a particle that feels the strong nuclear force.

concepts.name: Lepton
concepts.statement: A lepton is a fundamental particle that does not feel the strong nuclear force; the six leptons are the electron, muon and tau and their three neutrinos.

concepts.name: Baryon
concepts.statement: A baryon is a hadron that always decays to another baryon; it is made of three quarks.

concepts.name: Baryon number
concepts.statement: Baryon number $B$ is a quantum number equal to $+1$ for a baryon, $-1$ for an antibaryon and 0 for mesons and leptons.

concepts.name: Electron family number
concepts.statement: The electron family number $L_{e}$ is $+1$ for the electron and its neutrino, $-1$ for their antiparticles and 0 for every other particle.

concepts.name: Muon family number
concepts.statement: The muon family number $L_{\mu}$ is $+1$ for the muon and its neutrino, $-1$ for their antiparticles and 0 for every other particle.

concepts.name: Tau family number
concepts.statement: The tau family number $L_{\tau}$ is $+1$ for the tau and its neutrino, $-1$ for their antiparticles and 0 for every other particle.

concepts.name: Conservation of muon family number
terms: conservation of total muon family number
concepts.statement: In every reaction the total muon family number is conserved.

concepts.name: Conservation of strangeness
concepts.statement: Strangeness is conserved in reactions caused by the strong and electromagnetic forces but can change in reactions caused by the weak force.

concepts.name: Fundamental particles
concepts.statement: A fundamental particle is one with no substructure and no size beyond its wavelength. The known fundamental particles are of three types: the leptons, the quarks and the carrier particles.

concepts.name: Quark flavors
concepts.statement: The flavors are the six kinds of quark: up, down, strange, charm, bottom and top. Their charges are fractions of the proton's, $+\frac{2}{3}q_{e}$ for the up, charm and top quarks and $-\frac{1}{3}q_{e}$ for the down, strange and bottom quarks.

concepts.name: Quark composition of hadrons
concepts.statement: In the quark model every baryon is made of three quarks and every meson of a quark and an antiquark, rules that give hadrons only integral charges.

concepts.name: Finding quantum numbers from quarks
concepts.statement: A hadron's charge, baryon number and strangeness are found by adding those of its quarks, and working backward names the quarks of a particle from its quantum numbers.

concepts.name: Change of quark flavor
concepts.statement: The weak force can change the flavor of a quark, and the strong force cannot. Neutron decay is a down quark becoming an up quark, and the same change is why only the weak force can change strangeness.

concepts.name: Evidence for quarks
concepts.statement: No quark has been isolated, yet the evidence for quarks is strong: the $\Omega^{-}$ was found as the quark model predicted, high-energy electrons scatter from three pointlike charges inside the proton, and collisions produce jets of particles from single quarks.

concepts.name: Quark color and confinement
concepts.statement: Each quark carries one of three colors, and hadrons are always white, a baryon combining three colors and a meson a color and its anticolor. Color lets quarks in states such as $sss$ obey the exclusion principle and explains why a single quark cannot be isolated.

concepts.name: Three families
concepts.statement: Leptons, quarks and carrier particles each fall into three analogous families, normal, exotic and more exotic, and the particles of the higher families decay into those of the first.

concepts.name: Up quark
concepts.statement: The up quark is the quark flavor of charge $+\frac{2}{3}q_{e}$ in the first family; the proton is $uud$.

concepts.name: Down quark
concepts.statement: The down quark is the quark flavor of charge $-\frac{1}{3}q_{e}$ in the first family; the neutron is $udd$.

concepts.name: Strange quark
concepts.statement: The strange quark is the quark flavor of charge $-\frac{1}{3}q_{e}$ and strangeness $-1$ in the second family.

concepts.name: Charm quark
concepts.statement: The charm quark is the quark flavor of charge $+\frac{2}{3}q_{e}$ in the second family.

concepts.name: Bottom quark
concepts.statement: The bottom quark is the quark flavor of charge $-\frac{1}{3}q_{e}$ in the third family.

concepts.name: Top quark
concepts.statement: The top quark is the quark flavor of charge $+\frac{2}{3}q_{e}$ in the third family, by far the heaviest quark.

concepts.name: Color
concepts.statement: Color is a quantum number of quarks, with three values called red, green and blue, and their anticolors for antiquarks; it has nothing to do with visible color.

concepts.name: Quark confinement
concepts.statement: The theory of quark confinement holds that the force between quarks grows with their separation, so a single quark can never be isolated and quarks are found only in white combinations.

concepts.name: Quantum chromodynamics
concepts.statement: Quantum chromodynamics is the theory of the strong force between quarks, carried by gluons and acting on the quarks' color.

concepts.name: Electroweak theory
concepts.statement: Electroweak theory unifies the electromagnetic and weak forces, showing them to be one force at high energy. It predicted the $W^{\pm}$ and $Z^{0}$ and their masses before they were found.

concepts.name: Gluons and color
concepts.statement: Eight gluons carry the strong force between quarks and can change their color. Pion exchange between nucleons is, underneath, the exchange of quarks and gluons.

concepts.name: Standard Model
concepts.statement: The Standard Model is the combination of electroweak theory and quantum chromodynamics, the present theory of the fundamental particles and forces, with the Higgs boson its last predicted piece.

concepts.name: Grand Unified Theories
concepts.statement: A grand unified theory unifies the strong force with the electroweak force. Higher energy probes smaller distances, and at extremely high energies the strengths of the forces come together, far beyond the reach of any accelerator.

concepts.name: Proton decay
concepts.statement: Grand unified theories predict that the proton decays, as in $p \to \pi^{0} + e^{+}$, with a lifetime near $10^{31}$ y. Proton decay has not been observed, which constrains the theories.

concepts.name: Higgs boson
concepts.statement: The Higgs boson is a massive particle predicted by the Standard Model to explain why the other particles have mass, and found in 2012.

concepts.name: Superstring theory
concepts.statement: Superstring theory is a theory of everything based on vibrating strings some 10⁻³⁵ m in length, proposed to underlie all particles, forces, and space itself.
